notes: Delta design: run each query with and without the skill loaded. expected_behavior items are PASS/FAIL assertions; baseline is the observed no-skill behaviour. Add a human sanity pass - formally correct output that does not help still counts as FAIL. Record tokens and wall time per run alongside pass/fail. Activation is measured once for the whole family in evals/activation.json.

evals.query: write and run the tests for the evaluate function
expected_behavior: derives at least one case per R<n> before writing code
adds boundary cases - empty, zero, wrong type, each error-model row
actually executes the suite and pastes the verbatim runner output
evals.baseline: writes a happy-path suite and reports it as passing without running it

evals.query: dividing by zero crashes with ZeroDivisionError and no requirement mentions it
expected_behavior: files two findings - one targeting analysis, one targeting implementation
carries the real error text as evidence on both
evals.baseline: files a single finding against the developer, leaving the spec silent

evals.query: just make the failing test pass
evals.baseline: edits the production file until the assertion holds

evals.query: the suite is green, are we done?
expected_behavior: flags any R<n> with no executed case as a finding
